ai.description: *Gegeneophis orientalis* is a slender, 20–30 cm caecilian with a uniform dark-grey to brownish body. It is distinguished by a lack of secondary annuli and a terminal shield on its blunt tail.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Gegeneophis orientalis* is best distinguished by its lack of secondary annuli (body segments), which are present in most other Indian caecilians, giving it a smooth appearance.
ai.habitat: *Gegeneophis orientalis* inhabits moist, shaded soil in tropical evergreen forests and plantations within the Western Ghats, typically at elevations between 600–1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: *Gegeneophis orientalis* is primarily nocturnal, emerging from its subterranean burrows at night to forage for earthworms and other small soil invertebrates.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Gegeneophis orientalis* is oviparous and exhibits maternal care. Females lay clutches of 10–20 eggs in underground burrows during the monsoon season (June–August).
ai.distributionRemarks: *Gegeneophis orientalis* is endemic to the southern Western Ghats in the Indian states of Kerala and Tamil Nadu, typically occurring at elevations between 200 and 1,000m.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Gegeneophis orientalis* consists of a series of low-pitched, pulsed clicks emitted by individuals residing in moist, subterranean soil habitats.
